item.question: Cut long paper strips from waste paper. Give one strip (each of the same width) to each of your friends. Now, put the paper strip on your index finger and tear off the extra strip extending above your fingers. Paste these paper strips along the horizontal line in the given bar graph.
steps_tex: This is a hands-on activity. The sample below uses practice values, and your friends' strips will differ.
Cut five long strips of the same width, one for you and one for each of four friends.
Lay a strip on an index finger and tear off the extra part. Do this for each of the five fingers.
The sample strips are: Mine $6\text{ cm}$, Friend $1$ with $7\text{ cm}$, Friend $2$ with $5\text{ cm}$, Friend $3$ with $8\text{ cm}$ and Friend $4$ with $6\text{ cm}$.

Paste each strip standing up from the horizontal base, in its own place: Mine, then Friend $1$ to Friend $4$. The vertical line has $1\text{ cm}$ marked at the foot, so the top of a strip tells how long the strip is.
Check: the top of each strip meets its length on the vertical line, $6$, $7$, $5$, $8$ and $6$.
item.answer_tex: Sample answer (practice values): strips of $6$, $7$, $5$, $8$ and $6\text{ cm}$ for Mine and Friend $1$ to $4$. Your answer will differ.

The tallest bar is the longest index finger, so compare the tops of the bars on the vertical line.
The tops are at $6$, $7$, $5$, $8$ and $6$. The biggest number is $8$.
The bar that reaches $8\text{ cm}$ belongs to Friend $3$.
Check: $8$ is more than $6$, $7$, $5$ and $6$, and no other bar reaches $8$. Friend $3$ has the longest index finger.

concept_name: Using a Bar Graph: Totals and Predictions

item.question: A class collects old newspapers on five days (practice values): Monday 3 kg, Tuesday 6 kg, Wednesday 4 kg, Thursday 5 kg and Friday 2 kg. Find the highest day, the lowest day and the total. If 1 kg of newspaper makes 2 paper bags, how many bags can they make?
steps: Read each bar: Monday 3 kg, Tuesday 6 kg, Wednesday 4 kg, Thursday 5 kg and Friday 2 kg.
The tallest bar is Tuesday, so Tuesday is the highest, with 6 kg.
The shortest bar is Friday, so Friday is the lowest, with 2 kg.
Add all the bars for the total: 3 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 2 = 20 kg.
Use the rule on the total. 1 kg makes 2 bags, so the bags are 20 × 2 = 40.
Check by days: the days make 6, 12, 8, 10 and 4 bags, and 6 + 12 + 8 + 10 + 4 = 40.
item.answer: Highest Tuesday (6 kg), lowest Friday (2 kg), total 20 kg, and 20 × 2 = 40 bags
item.text:
Worked example: A class collects old newspapers on five days (practice values): Monday 3 kg, Tuesday 6 kg, Wednesday 4 kg, Thursday 5 kg and Friday 2 kg. Find the highest day, the lowest day and the total. If 1 kg of newspaper makes 2 paper bags, how many bags can they make?
1. Read each bar: Monday 3 kg, Tuesday 6 kg, Wednesday 4 kg, Thursday 5 kg and Friday 2 kg.
2. The tallest bar is Tuesday, so Tuesday is the highest, with 6 kg.
3. The shortest bar is Friday, so Friday is the lowest, with 2 kg.
4. Add all the bars for the total: 3 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 2 = 20 kg.
5. Use the rule on the total. 1 kg makes 2 bags, so the bags are 20 × 2 = 40.
6. Check by days: the days make 6, 12, 8, 10 and 4 bags, and 6 + 12 + 8 + 10 + 4 = 40.
Answer: Highest Tuesday (6 kg), lowest Friday (2 kg), total 20 kg, and 20 × 2 = 40 bags
